'''Jean Giraud''' ({{IPA|fr|ʒiʁo|lang}}; 2 February 1936 – 27 or 28 March 2007)<ref name=BNF/><ref name="dh">[http://www.ens-lyon.fr/ENSinfo//ENSinfo04-07.html "Un dernier hommage à Jean Giraud"] {{webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081014221257/http://www.ens-lyon.fr/ENSinfo//ENSinfo04-07.html |date=14 October 2008 }}, Philippe Gillet, ''ENS Info'' 70, April 2007.</ref> was a French mathematician, a student of [[Alexander Grothendieck]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=130210|name=Jean Giraud}}</ref> His research focused on non-abelian [[cohomology]] and the theory of [[topos|topoi]]. In particular, he authored the book ''Cohomologie non-abélienne'' (Springer, 1971) and proved the theorem that bears his name, which gives a characterization of a [[Grothendieck topos]].<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ncatlab.org/nlab/show/Giraud%27s+theorem | title=Giraud's theorem |website=nlab | date=13 November 2021}}</ref>

From 1969 to 1989, he was a professor at [[École normale supérieure de Saint-Cloud]].<ref name=BNF/>

From 1993 to 1994, he was deputy director for research of [[École normale supérieure de Lyon]], where he was made interim director in 1994 and director from 1995 to 2000.<ref name="dh"/>
